newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco to push deals with private sector-new CEO.
newsitem.headline: Codelco to push deals with private sector-new CEO.

text.p: Chilean state copper company Codelco will continue to improve its management and give strong emphasis to joint ventures with private firms, said the corporation's new CEO Marcos Lima who took office Monday.
"We aim to improve management in all senses and give a strong push to associations with the private sector," Lima told reporters after a seminar on Codelco's role in Chile's economic development.
Codelco, the world's largest copper producer, built the recently opened El Abra copper mine with Cyprus Amax Minerals and has a number of exploration programs with foreign mining firms.
Lima, formerly Codelco's vice president of finance and administration, replaced Juan Villarzu who took office as President Eduardo Frei's chief-of-staff at the weekend.
Asked if Codelco is concerned by the tumble in world copper prices this year, Lima replied: "Of course, it's normal that in a company like ours we are worried about the issue."
Lima said senior Codelco officials would go to Britain next week to hold talks on ways of giving copper producers a greater say in the way the London Metals Exchange operates.
Codelco expects fine copper production to rise to 1.5 million tonnes by the end of the decade from 1.2 million tonnes last year, he said.

Largest increases will be at the Chuquicamata mine with output rising to 666,000 tonnes against 610,000 tonnes last year and Andina where output will increase to 247,000 tonnes from 146,000 tonnes in 1995.
The new Radomiro Tomic pit, which will start operating in 1998, will mine 150,000 tonnes of copper a year.
